The (Ga,Fe)N layers were grown by metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy (MOVPE) on GaN buffer layers deposited on c-plane sapphire substrates.
Sample A contains both α-Fe and γ'-GayFe4-yN nanocrystals, while Sample B and the annealed Sample A* (A*) contain only the γ'-GayFe4-yN phase.
The size of the nanocrystals is estimated to be 17±2 nm for α-Fe and 22±2 nm for γ'-GayFe4-yN from the HRXRD analysis.
The magnetic response of the layers is dominated by a superparamagnetic-like behavior from the nanocrystals and a paramagnetic contribution from dilute Fe3+ ions in the GaN matrix.
The coercive field values observed (10-60 mT) are consistent with the presence of ferromagnetic γ'-Fe4N nanoparticles.
The resistivity of Sample B is enhanced by about 3 orders of magnitude below 100K compared to the other samples, attributed to the diffusion of dilute Fe into the GaN capping layer.
The transition from Arrhenius-type to Mott variable-range hopping conduction occurs between 50-25K for Samples A, A*, and GaN, and between 130-100K for Sample B.
The Mott hopping temperature (T0Mott) values obtained are in good agreement with previous reports for Gd-doped GaN and GaN.
Sample A* shows a hysteretic behavior in the magnetoresistance at low fields (<1T) and low temperatures (<25K), related to the spin polarization of the embedded nanocrystals.
All samples containing the (Ga,Fe)N layers exhibit a positive anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) over the entire temperature range, which is not observed in the GaN reference layer.
